title: How many pebbles does the riddle hold?
description: A riddle about pebbles that leave one over in twos, in threes and in fives, and none over in sevens, with fewer than one hundred. The video takes the one away, finds the multiples of thirty, and tests each in sevens.
teaching_notes: One idea: take the common remainder away, then test the few numbers left against the last condition. Watch for students who stop at thirty one or sixty one without testing sevens.

source: Figure it Out (multiples and remainders, question 5)
video_script.why: The student can find numbers with a common remainder on several divisors and now adds a last condition that picks one of them.
video_script.substitution: Take the one extra pebble away, use multiples of thirty, put the one back, then test each in groups of seven.
video_script.anchor: a handful of pebbles in groups, the riddle in the Figure it Out of the book
video_script.payoff_line: The riddle holds ninety one pebbles
maths_rules: n - 1 is a multiple of 2, 3 and 5, so a multiple of 30
n = 30k + 1 below 100: 31, 61, 91; the next, 121, is too many
1 pebble leaves 1 in groups of 7, so it does not fit
video_script.design: One handful of pebbles. The extra pebble is set aside, the rest groups exactly in twos, threes and fives, then each candidate is tested in sevens.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a handful of pebbles; groups of 3, 2 and 5 each with 1 pebble left; groups of 7 with none left; fewer than 100

marks.groups: the pebbles group in threes, in twos and in fives, each time with one left
marks.sevens: the pebbles group in sevens with none left, and the words fewer than 100 appear
marks.ask: a blank box for the number of pebbles appears

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a riddle from your book.
<bookmark mark='pebbles'/>Someone holds some pebbles, and not too many.
<bookmark mark='groups'/>In threes, one pebble is left. In twos, one is left. In fives, one is left.
<bookmark mark='sevens'/>In sevens, none is left, and there are fewer than one hundred pebbles.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many pebbles are there?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a handful of pebbles; 1 pebble set aside; the rest in full groups of 2, of 3 and of 5

marks.same: the words the same way as the example in your book appear
marks.aside: one pebble slides away from the handful
marks.rest: the rest forms full groups of two, of three and of five

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book.
Take the common remainder away.
<bookmark mark='aside'/>Here, set the one extra pebble aside.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>What is left makes full groups of two, of three and of five.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1 left over in groups of 2, 3 and 5; none left over in groups of 7; fewer than 100 pebbles

marks.sevens: the other two conditions are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one pebble is left in groups of two, three and five.
<bookmark mark='sevens'/>No pebble is left in groups of seven, and there are fewer than one hundred.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of pebbles

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number of pebbles.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: take 1 away: n - 1 is a multiple of 2, of 3 and of 5

marks.take: n minus one is written under the number n
marks.all: the words multiple of 2, of 3 and of 5 appear beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step one, take away the one extra pebble.
<bookmark mark='all'/>What is left is a multiple of two, of three and of five.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: multiples of 30: 30, 60, 90; put 1 back: 31, 61, 91; the next, 121, is too many

marks.thirty: the words multiples of thirty appear
marks.list: thirty, sixty and ninety are written
marks.back: one is added to each, giving thirty one, sixty one and ninety one
marks.next: one hundred twenty one appears and is crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='thirty'/>Step two, the numbers that two, three and five all divide are the multiples of thirty.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Below one hundred, these are thirty, sixty and ninety.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Put the one pebble back to get thirty one, sixty one and ninety one.
<bookmark mark='next'/>The next one, one hundred twenty one, is too many.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: groups of 7: 31 = 7 x 4 + 3; 61 = 7 x 8 + 5; 91 = 7 x 13; 1 pebble leaves 1 over

marks.thirtyone: thirty one is split into four sevens with three over
marks.sixtyone: sixty one is split into eight sevens with five over
marks.ninetyone: ninety one is split into thirteen sevens with none over
marks.one: one pebble is shown with one over in sevens and crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='thirtyone'/>Step three, test each in groups of seven. Thirty one is four sevens and three over.
<bookmark mark='sixtyone'/>Sixty one is eight sevens and five over.
<bookmark mark='ninetyone'/>Ninety one is thirteen sevens, with none over.
<bookmark mark='one'/>One pebble also leaves one over in sevens, so it does not fit.

marks.twos: ninety one is split in twos, threes and fives, each with one over
marks.sevens: ninety one is split in sevens with none over

narration: <bookmark mark='twos'/>Step four, put the number back in the riddle. Ninety one is two times forty five plus one, and three times thirty plus one.
<bookmark mark='sevens'/>It is five times eighteen plus one, and seven times thirteen exactly.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The riddle holds ninety one pebbles.
